content.comment_body: Hello everyone, this is my first post here. I have three [product_name] modules ([version_no]) connected via a network switch. My goal is to transfer the state of a digital input from one [product_name] to another. I'm programming in LAD and can't use the automatic connection creator from [product_name] engineering software, as it's only available in FBD language. IP addresses are set up for each PLC. In LAD, I tried configuring Network Output for one module (for example 192.168.0.2), but I can't read this Output in another module (for example 192.168.0.3) when I configure it for Network Input. Could someone explain what TSAP means? I appreciate any help.
Hi [user_name], thanks for your quick response—the solution is clear now. I uploaded your example files to my PLCs and everything works! Thanks again for your assistance.

analysis.insight_summary: The user faced difficulties setting up network communication between three [product_name] modules using LAD language within [product_name] engineering software. They struggled to transfer a digital input state from one module to another due to the lack of an automatic connection setup tool for LAD, which is only available for FBD. This prompted questions about configuration terms like TSAP and the proper network I/O procedure. Another user's example project quickly resolved the issue, highlighting the need for better documentation and cross-language support in the software.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to easily exchange digital inputs between modules, regardless of programming language used. They also anticipate having straightforward instructions or built-in tools in the engineering software for these tasks, as well as clearer explanations of technical terms like TSAP required for network configuration.
